title: Weighted noise identities
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $w_i\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $\sum_i w_i=1$, and let $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ and $f,g:I\to\mathbb{R}$. Write $m_f=\sum_i w_i f_i$ and $m_g=\sum_i w_i g_i$. Then both identities hold:
\[
\sum_i w_i\bigl(\rho g_i+(1-\rho)m_g\bigr)^2=\rho^2\sum_i w_i g_i^2+(1-\rho^2)m_g^2,
\qquad
\sum_i w_i\bigl(\rho f_i+(1-\rho)m_f\bigr)g_i=\sum_i w_i f_i\bigl(\rho g_i+(1-\rho)m_g\bigr).
\]
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, let real weights satisfy $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $\rho\in\bbr$. For real vectors $f,g$, write $m_h=\sum_iw_ih_i$ and $(T_\rho h)_i=\rho h_i+(1-\rho)m_h$. Then $\sum_iw_i(T_\rho g)_i^2=\rho^2\sum_iw_ig_i^2+(1-\rho^2)m_g^2$ and $\sum_iw_i(T_\rho f)_ig_i=\sum_iw_if_i(T_\rho g)_i$.
